itemsTotal.description: §3.13: rows in this answer's registry view — the whole registry, or the rows matching the [type] filter.

pools.description: every swap venue the mirror knows; an empty array is a legal answer

description.description: `--full` only from 0.5.0 (§3.13). 18.9 KB of the item registry's 50 KB is description prose, byte for byte the same on every call.

for.description: §3.13 (0.5.0): who the item is FOR — KAMI / ACCOUNT / …. Omitted when the world holds no target.

pools.description: swap venues trading this item; an empty array means none

effects.description: §3.12 (enrich): what USE and EQUIP allocate, one row per raw allo.

requirements.description: §3.12 (enrich): what USE requires. Empty array = the registry stores no USE condition.

Pool.description: A constant-product swap venue between two items. Facts only: reserves, fee, share supply, creation time. No swap quote is served — see impliedRate.

items.description: the traded pair, item registry indices, low index first

reserves.description: reserve held of each item, positionally aligned to items

impliedRate.description: PURE RESERVE RATIO — fee-exclusive and impact-exclusive. A valuation of current depth, NOT a swap quote: a real swap moves along the curve and pays feeBps. Omitted when either reserve is zero.

AlloText.description: The pinned client's own interpretation of one allocation, projected to {name, description}. `image` is never served: two shapes files carry the module NAMESPACE of a png import there rather than a URL (SPEC §4.1 quirk 2).

AlloOut.description: One RAW allocation the world stores (type, index, value) with the pinned client's interpretation of it beside it. Grouped per raw allo deliberately: the interpreter fans out — a BONUS allo yields one entry per bonus, a droptable allo one consolidated entry — so a flat parsed list would have no positional correspondence to what the world holds. `entries` is empty when this pin interprets the shape not at all; the raw facts still stand.

ItemRequirement.description: One USE requirement: the raw condition target plus the pinned client's interpreted text. Grouped rather than a bare string because 48 of the 53 item conditions at this pin are KAMI_CAN_EAT with index 0, whose text is the single word "None" — indistinguishable, without the target beside it, from a real requirement. Text is verbatim, upstream spacing quirks included.

value.description: VERBATIM, as a string (§1.2). A condition's value is not always a count — a room gate's is an entity id, and Number() on an id-sized uint returns 2.65e+76: a value the world does not hold and nothing can join on.

ItemFlags.description: Registry flags the world stores on the item.
